segments.label: Durable HTTP history and duplicate suppression

messages.label: Socket closes / eventually times out
messages.note: Node A was killed; its queues and shared tails are lost, not committed messages.

messages.label: Client retries with capped exponential jitter
messages.note: Base 100 ms doubles up to 10 s; each delay is in [base/2, base).

messages.label: resume: last processed contiguous cursor
messages.note: Device cursor is independent of Node A's last enqueued position.

Authorized head; cursor not beyond it
resumed; socket reader buffers live events
Recovery HTTP can reach another replica
Fresh membership/head; history on cache miss
HTTP page through Nginx; merge with live events
messages.note: Drop sequence <= cursor; gaps recover again; advance only after callback success.

Ordered WS messages / current read events
Client 1 s HTTP catch-up also repairs gaps
Presence operation: prune expired leases

cards.title: Who recovers what
items: Client owns reconnect, jitter, HTTP catch-up, duplicate suppression and processed cursors.
Each surviving app owns shared-feed reconciliation and bounded WS delivery.
Register/resume first, then HTTP catch-up: live/history overlap is expected.
Server and client both reconcile every second; neither needs every Redis hint.

cards.title: Durability and receipts
items: Acknowledged messages already committed with outbox and sequence in PostgreSQL.
Lost-ack retries reuse the client message ID; identical payload returns original result.
Read positions are durable; resume emits current receipts and GET /receipts restores them.
The sample Go client processes messages but ignores live read-event frames.

cards.title: Multiple devices and failure limits
items: One 30 s Redis lease per connection; pongs renew after server pings every 10 s.
A killed node cannot clean up; expired leases are pruned on Redis presence operations.
Other device leases keep the user online; last_seen is last observed activity.
Cursor memory is not persisted by the sample client; restarting it can replay from zero.

cards.title: Not database/cache high availability
items: This path assumes PostgreSQL, Redis and Nginx are reachable while one app dies.
PostgreSQL outage: sends cannot acknowledge; retries wait for recovery.
Redis outage: HTTP history/sends can work, but presence/new WS setup is unavailable.
No dependency replica, distributed cursor store or automatic database failover exists.
The proxy never retries an uncertain POST; recovery and send retries belong to the client.

cards.title: Sequence scope
items: B/C represents surviving processes; an HTTP request need not hit the WS process.
Healthy-app messages to the device travel through Nginx; forwarding hops are abbreviated.
Periodic repair and lease operations are independent; vertical placement is illustrative order, not measured time.
Code-inspected working files are recorded in implementation-evidence.json; no commit-pinned source claim.
